clue.text: Bent cycle had to be carried

parts.note: a cycle is a round, as in a round of talks or duties
something carried on the shoulders has been shouldered

explanation.surface: A bicycle got buckled, so its owner had to carry it home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' looks like a description of the buckled cycle, but it is the definition: stooping, with the shoulders hunched forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a stooped, hunched posture is described as bent in that way.

clue.text: What the subeditor did about repetition, say

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: say signals that the word for repetition is heard, giving a word spoken the same way

parts.note: learning by rote is learning by repetition

explanation.surface: A subeditor queries a writer's repetitiveness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' means the preceding word is heard: ROTE sounds like WROTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A subeditor's job includes rewriting copy, so what one did is the past tense of that.

clue.text: Trouble in horsy section of society

parts.note: up can mean in, as being up at university means being in residence
the horsy set is the hunting and riding circle of society

explanation.surface: A scandal disturbs the equestrian social circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a link word here but UP.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouble someone is to upset them, a synonym as a verb.

clue.text: Groom, dejected, gets reprimand

parts.note: to groom is to dress, as with hair or a horse
a dejected person is down

explanation.surface: A gloomy bridegroom gets a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' suggests a bridegroom, but it is a verb here: to dress.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress someone down is an idiom meaning to scold them severely.

clue.text: Pay attention to judge

explanation.definitionFit: To hear is to listen to someone, and a judge hears a case in court.

clue.text: Nudes are concealed below the surface

indicators.note: concealed suggests the letters of nudes are rearranged out of sight into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Naked swimmers stay hidden underwater.
explanation.definitionFit: Undersea means beneath the surface of the sea, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Fancy dress initially takes lots of paper

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of dress

parts.note: a ream is a large quantity of paper, 500 sheets

explanation.surface: A fancy-dress costume needs a lot of paper to make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy dress' reads as one phrase, but 'Fancy' alone is the definition, a noun meaning a daydream.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a whimsical imagining, a flight of fantasy, as a dream is.

clue.text: Being damned in report by head produces a very red face

indicators.note: in report means the word for damned is heard rather than written

parts.note: ruddy is a mild British euphemism for bloody or damned
a ness is a headland

explanation.surface: Being cursed in a report from the boss leaves someone flushed with embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' joins on as a link; 'in report' turns RUDDY into its sound-alike RUDDI, and NESS is a headland, as in Loch Ness's neighbouring capes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruddiness is a reddish, flushed complexion, the quality of having a very red face.

clue.text: Wealthy old woman encouraged to bet

parts.note: do is an urging word, as in do come in, said to encourage
to bet is to wager

explanation.surface: A rich elderly lady is urged to have a flutter.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'encouraged to bet' as the exhortation 'Do wager!'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow holding a title or property from her late husband, typically a wealthy elderly lady.

clue.text: Useless tract gave title to poet

explanation.surface: A barren stretch of land inspired a poet's choice of title.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition refers to T. S. Eliot's famous 1922 poem of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: A barren, unusable stretch of ground is called this; it is also the title of Eliot's landmark poem.

clue.text: Give permanent income to old wife after death

indicators.note: after means old wife come behind death

parts.note: death is the end of life
W is the standard abbreviation for wife, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A will settles a pension on an old widow once someone dies.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow a person or institution is to provide a lasting fund or income for them.

clue.text: Slow to use book that's translated

indicators.note: translated means the letters of to use and the book letter are turned into another form

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A reader finds a translated book heavy going to use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slow' means slow-witted here, not slow-moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse describes someone dull or slow to understand, a synonym in the mental sense.

clue.text: Stuffing in which to pack china

parts.note: to cram is to pack tightly
Ming is the classic Chinese porcelain

explanation.surface: Packing material is used to protect fine porcelain in a crate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'china' is not a crockery word for packing here but MING, the dynasty famous for porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuffing something full is cramming it, a direct synonym in the gerund form.

clue.text: Occupy centre of assembly by ruse

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letters, here the two middle letters of assembly

parts.note: a ruse is a ploy, a cunning stratagem

explanation.surface: Activists take over a meeting hall by trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' takes EM, the middle two letters of the eight-letter 'assembly'.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ someone or something is to keep them occupied or busy, a synonym.

clue.text: Old patients ready for a quiz show

parts.note: before the NHS, panel patients were those on a doctor's list under National Insurance
game means ready or willing, as in game for anything

explanation.surface: Elderly patients are keen to take part in a TV quiz.
explanation.walkthrough: Before 1948 British workers insured under National Insurance were on a doctor's panel, so old patients make PANEL.
explanation.definitionFit: A panel game is a television or radio quiz with a team of celebrity contestants.

clue.text: Sort of clothing that makes soldiers curse

parts.note: soldiers, especially private soldiers, are men
to curse is to swear

explanation.surface: A uniform so uncomfortable that the troops start cursing.
explanation.definitionFit: Menswear is the category of clothing made for men, a kind of attire.

clue.text: Take car by rail, where you pay a bit more for comfort

definitions.text: where you pay a bit more for comfort

parts.note: a saloon is a type of car with a closed body
a bar is a rail, as on a fence

explanation.surface: Travelling by train in first class costs extra for comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: A saloon bar is the more comfortable room in a British pub, where drinks used to cost a little more; 'Take' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A saloon bar is the plusher lounge of a British pub, where prices were traditionally higher.

clue.text: He loves a decorative piece

parts.note: fancy means decorative or ornate
a chess or draughts piece is a man

explanation.surface: Someone adores an ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' is a game counter, a man in chess or draughts.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy man is a woman's lover, so he is the one who loves her.

clue.text: Church rules not applicable to lay readers?

definitions.text: Church rules not applicable to lay readers?

parts.words: Church rules not applicable to lay readers?
parts.note: a joke reading: laws for clergymen called canons, which would not apply to lay readers, who are laymen

explanation.surface: Ecclesiastical regulations that exempt lay readers in the parish.
explanation.walkthrough: Lay readers are non-clergy who lead services; the joke takes the term as rules for canons, the clergy, rather than the church's whole body of law.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of ecclesiastical law governing a church goes by this name.

clue.text: Temps in informal gear

explanation.definitionFit: Casual workers hired temporarily are casuals, and so are relaxed everyday clothes.

clue.text: Stuffy duke shut up

parts.note: stuffy weather or air is close

explanation.surface: An airless aristocrat is told to stop talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shut up' looks like an order to be quiet, but it is the definition as an adjective: locked or closed down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shut up, like a house for the winter, is closed.

clue.text: Tie-breaker game interrupted by some police

indicators.note: interrupted by means the police letters break into the word for game

parts.note: deer are game animals, hunted for sport
the CID, Criminal Investigation Department, is a branch of the British police

explanation.surface: A tie-break match is held up by police officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game' looks like a sports match but is game animals, deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A decider is a final game played to settle a tie.

clue.text: Closest I may come to turning point

indicators.note: the letters of closest I may come out as a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone admits this is the nearest they will get to a decisive moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The solstice is when the sun appears to turn back at its northernmost or southernmost point, so it is literally a turning point.
explanation.definitionFit: Solstice comes from the sun appearing to stand still and turn back, making it an astronomical turning point.

clue.text: Foolish fellow molested pert wife

indicators.note: molested means the letters of pert and the wife letter are disturbed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An idiot harasses a cheeky married woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A twerp is a silly or contemptible person, a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: Artistic design: one of Grandma's?

explanation.surface: A decorative pattern among a grandmother's handicrafts.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on Grandma Moses, the American folk painter: something of Moses is Mosaic, as in Mosaic law.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture made of small coloured tiles is one; the word also means relating to Moses.

clue.text: A sea can be powerfully poetic

parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the open sea

explanation.surface: The ocean can be a mighty subject for poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poetic' tells you the word is archaic or literary: amain means with full force.
explanation.definitionFit: Amain is a literary adverb meaning with great force or at full speed.

clue.text: Temporary irregularity putting bishop on edge

indicators.note: putting on means the bishop letter goes before the edge word in this down clue
putting on means the bishop letter goes before the edge word in this down clue

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bishop in chess notation
a lip is an edge or rim

explanation.surface: A churchman is pushed to the brink of a temporary wobble.
explanation.definitionFit: A blip is a brief, temporary deviation from a normal trend.

clue.text: Degrade a headquarters

parts.note: a military base serves as headquarters

explanation.surface: Demoting a regimental HQ.
explanation.definitionFit: To abase someone is to lower or humiliate them, a synonym for degrade.

clue.text: Works committee giving publication firm backing

parts.note: a works, a factory, is a mill
a board is a governing committee

explanation.surface: A factory committee gives a publishing company financial support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like financial support, but it is the stiff board used for the covers, or backing, of books.
explanation.definitionFit: Millboard is a thick pasteboard used by bookbinders to stiffen book covers.

clue.text: A capital provider, though always out

definitions.text: A capital provider, though always out

parts.words: A capital provider, though always out
parts.note: a business investor who supplies money but takes no active part, read as someone permanently unconscious

explanation.surface: An investor who funds a firm but is never around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'always out' suggests absence, and also being dead to the world, asleep: such an investor plays no part in running the business.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the term for a partner who puts in capital but takes no active role in management.
